_doc: VERIFY-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-21): lessons from formally verified and critical-infrastructure code, applied as checks. Every invariant names the model that checks it (foundation/verify.py), the property, the code conformance probe or runtime monitor that ties the model to the deployed code, and its source. Read by foundation/verify.py; `python3 -m foundation verify --check` runs in `checks`. Coverage = invariants model-checked and tied to code / all invariants, written to ops/verification.json.

sources.tla-aws: C. Newcombe et al., How Amazon Web Services Uses Formal Methods, CACM 58(4), 2015
sources.sel4: G. Klein et al., seL4: Formal Verification of an OS Kernel, SOSP 2009 (proof tied to the implementation)
sources.compcert: X. Leroy, Formal verification of a realistic compiler, CACM 52(7), 2009
sources.power-of-ten: G. Holzmann, The Power of Ten: Rules for Developing Safety-Critical Code, IEEE Computer 39(6), 2006 (rule 2: bounded loops; rule 5: assertions)
sources.do-178c: RTCA DO-178C, Software Considerations in Airborne Systems (requirements-to-test traceability)
sources.quickcheck: K. Claessen, J. Hughes, QuickCheck: property-based testing, ICFP 2000
sources.ashby: W. R. Ashby, Design for a Brain, 1952
